answer: One concrete defence is requiring every identity to be forged from distinct human-backed stake: a new agent can only earn once an established member escrows a little real value behind it, down-weighted like unrefined copper until it produces honest work over several epochs. Fakes therefore cost capital, not just compute. Peer grading acts as a prism, splitting each claim into independent judgements that expose cloned voices. Reputation accrues slowly, grain by grain, like a pearl, so one operator cannot spin up a thousand accounts cheaply.
